Chapter 9: Wealth, Charity, and the Ethics of Earning
Have you ever noticed how money tends to reveal what really matters to us? Whether it's at the market, around the dinner table, or in those quiet moments when we feel moved to give, the way we handle our wealth truly shapes the world around us.
Sunan Abu Dawud is full of stories that dig deep into the ethics of earning, spending, and giving. These stories remind us: faith doesn’t just live in our hearts—it’s also reflected in our wallets.
Picture a merchant, tempted to take a shortcut. He remembers the Prophet’s warning against dishonesty. Now, he could easily cheat and no one would notice, but instead, he chooses honesty—the tougher road. Over time, his reputation grows, and his business becomes a pillar of trust for the whole community.
Meanwhile, imagine a family gathered together, debating how much they should give in charity. The traditions encourage them to be generous, but also to find balance—not to give so much that they end up struggling themselves. The Prophet’s own example is one of moderation, kindness, and a strong sense of responsibility for others.
There’s a story of a wealthy man who gives openly, hoping for praise. Then, there’s someone else who gives quietly, wanting only to please God. What really counts, these traditions teach us, isn’t the size of the gift, but the intention behind it—and the difference it makes to someone in need.
But the ethics of wealth go even further. These stories talk about paying fair wages, keeping honest contracts, and always following through on promises. There are warnings against greed and exploitation, and reminders about the risks of letting money become the thing we worship.
The truth is, a lot of people don’t realize just how practical these teachings are—or how much they can shape our everyday lives. The stories invite us to see wealth not as the goal, but as a tool—a way to build trust, support others, and live with real integrity.
If you’re navigating the twists and turns of modern finance, these traditions from Sunan Abu Dawud offer timeless wisdom. Every transaction, every decision about money, is an opportunity. It’s a chance to act with honesty, compassion, and generosity, turning even the most ordinary moments into acts of faith.
